name: Dabrafenib
route_note: oral capsules twice daily, usually with trametinib; dispersible tablets for children

discovery.note: A thiazole-based ATP-competitive inhibitor selective for mutant BRAF.

tagline: BRAF inhibitor paired with trametinib for melanoma and tumour-agnostic BRAF V600E use
summary: Dabrafenib is an oral inhibitor of mutant BRAF kinase. Combined with the MEK inhibitor trametinib it is a standard treatment for BRAF V600-mutant melanoma (metastatic and adjuvant), lung and anaplastic thyroid cancer, paediatric low-grade glioma, and any solid tumour with a BRAF V600E mutation.
mechanism: Dabrafenib competitively binds the ATP pocket of mutant BRAF V600E/K/D, inhibiting MEK and ERK phosphorylation and causing G1 arrest and apoptosis in BRAF-dependent tumours.

As with other first-generation BRAF inhibitors it can paradoxically activate MAPK signalling in BRAF wild-type cells; co-administration of trametinib suppresses this, reducing cutaneous squamous tumours and delaying resistance.
uses: BRAF V600E/K-mutant unresectable or metastatic melanoma (with trametinib, or alone)
Adjuvant treatment of resected stage III BRAF-mutant melanoma (with trametinib)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Dabrafenib (Tafinlar) and trametinib (Mekinist) approved as single agents on the same day for BRAF-mutant melanoma.

history.title: Combination approval
history.detail: Accelerated approval of dabrafenib plus trametinib, the first BRAF/MEK combination.

history.title: Novartis transaction
history.detail: GSK's oncology portfolio, including dabrafenib, is transferred to Novartis.

history.title: Adjuvant melanoma and thyroid
history.detail: COMBI-AD leads to adjuvant approval; anaplastic thyroid cancer also approved.

history.title: Tumour-agnostic
history.detail: FDA grants accelerated approval for BRAF V600E-mutant solid tumours.

history.title: Paediatric glioma
history.detail: Approval for BRAF V600E paediatric low-grade glioma with new paediatric formulations.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP2C8 and CYP3A4 to active hydroxy- and desmethyl-dabrafenib; induces CYP3A4

facts: Pyrexia is more frequent with the dabrafenib–trametinib combination than with either drug alone.
